timeline.event: Whole-genome resequencing of 110 accessions indicates that Cannabis sativa was first domesticated in East Asia in early Neolithic times.
The US Marihuana Tax Act of 1937 burdened cannabis cultivation, including fiber hemp.
The US government released the film Hemp for Victory urging farmers to grow hemp for rope and cordage while imported fibers were scarce.
The 2018 Farm Bill defined hemp as Cannabis sativa with no more than 0.3% delta-9 THC on a dry weight basis, separating it from marijuana in federal law.
World production of hemp fiber and tow was about 60,000 tonnes, about 1.7% of natural fibers and about 0.05% of all textile fibers.

timeline.event: Dundee spinners learned to soften raw Bengal jute with a whale oil and water emulsion so it could run on machinery built for flax.
The first jute mill in Bengal opened at Rishra on the Hooghly River near Calcutta.
Bengal mills overtook the Scottish jute industry, moving manufacture to the region where the crop was grown.
A life cycle study from Indian researchers reported net negative greenhouse gas results for jute and kenaf carrier bags by crediting carbon taken up during crop growth.

timeline.event: A 2020 review dates the first PET fiber, Terylene, to 1941, developed in Britain three years after nylon was launched.
The first commercially marketed polyester fiber reached consumers in men's suits blending DuPont's fiber with worsted wool.
Demand for DuPont's polyester, developed in a pilot plant at Seaford, Delaware, led to construction of a plant at Kinston, North Carolina.
A laundering study quantified the mass of microfibers released by machine-washing new and aged synthetic garments.
Polyester made up about 59% of global fiber output, roughly 78 million tonnes.

timeline.event: Wallace Carothers's group at DuPont made the polyamide that became nylon 6,6.
DuPont began commercial nylon production at Seaford, Delaware, on 15 December 1939.
Nylon stockings went on sale nationally in the United States on 15 May 1940, after a limited release in Wilmington in October 1939.
The American Chemical Society designated the Seaford plant a National Historic Chemical Landmark.
Aquafil began regenerating nylon 6 waste to caprolactam in Ljubljana, Slovenia, under the ECONYL name, according to the producer.
Polyamide output reached about 7 million tonnes, about 5% of global fiber production.
